title: Impact of praeoperative Barium swallow fluoroscopy on surgical decision in bariatric revision and REDO surgery
summary:
Obesity is a rapidly increasing disease worldwide, for which bariatric surgery currently represents the most effective therapy. Standard procedures such as sleeve gastrectomy or Roux-en-Y gastric bypass lead to significant weight loss and improvement in metabolic comorbidities, but are associated with long-term complications such as reflux, hiatal hernias (thoracic sleeve or thoracic pouch), anastomotic leaks, passage disorders, sleeve gastrectomy dilatations, dumping syndrome, or weight regain. Precise diagnostics are crucial, especially before planned revision surgeries, to identify relevant findings early and to optimally plan the surgical strategy.

In addition to state-of-the-art surgical procedures and an interdisciplinary therapeutic approach, the center is particularly distinguished by its targeted use of barium swallow fluoroscopy (BSF) – a dynamic imaging technique that plays a central role in the diagnosis of late post-bariatric complications.

BSF allows for a precise functional assessment of the esophagus, stomach, and proximal small intestine. Following oral administration of barium sulfate, the movement of the contrast agent is recorded in real time. The examination is performed with the patient standing, and the gastroesophageal junction is specifically visualized. This procedure enables the differentiated assessment of changes following gastric bypass surgery (Roux-en-Y bypass RYGB, single-anastomosis gastric bypass OAGB), sleeve gastrectomy, banded procedures, and revision surgeries such as SASI (Single Anastomosis Sleeve Ileal Bypass) and SADI-S (Single Anastomosis Duodeno-Ileal Bypass with Sleeve). Particularly in cases of late complications such as anastomotic stenosis or dilatation, fistula formation, delayed gastric emptying, reflux, sleeve gastrectomy dilatation, or indirect indications of dumping syndrome, BSF provides crucial diagnostic information that often cannot be captured with comparable detail using static methods such as CT or MRI.

BSF is an integral part of the center's diagnostic spectrum and complements esophagogastroduodenoscopy (EGD), which is established as the standard procedure for detecting mucosal pathologies. The combination of both procedures provides maximum diagnostic accuracy. Diagnostic certainty is achieved, which is crucial for choosing the appropriate revision or REDO procedure. The results are directly incorporated into treatment planning – be it for surgical decisions, endoscopic intervention, drug therapy, or adjustments to nutritional therapy.

This project retrospectively evaluates the findings of patients who underwent both esophagogastroduodenoscopy (EGD) and bariatric fluoroscopy (BFS) after primary or revision bariatric surgery. The study aims to determine the sensitivity and specificity of BFS, taking into account clinical symptoms and intraoperative findings. Furthermore, it investigates the extent to which BFS influences the choice of the planned surgical procedure.
conditions: Diaphragmatic hernia with obstruction, without gangrene

interventions.name: Patients who underwent planned bariatric surgery at the obesity center and received barium swallow fluoroscopy between November 2023 and November 2025 will be retrospectively identified.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patient: Individuals who underwent primary or revision bariatric surgery within the specified period.
Preoperative barium swallow fluoroscopy and esophagogastroduodenoscopy are performed.
Findings are fully documented in the patient's medical record.
Age >18 years
Exclusion criteria:
Missing documentation of barium swallow fluoroscopy or esophagogastroduodenoscopy/gastroscopy

Patient: under 18 years of age
